LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can you make your composition interesting to read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions
2. create an open- ended composition on a variety of themes

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. List topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions,
2. Discuss in groups ideas and experiences on a given topic,
3. Proofread the composition and make necessary corrections, 1. How can you make your composition interesting to read? 2. Why is it important to proofread your composition? 18
4. Creativity and Imagination: The learner organises ideas as they create compositions based on a variety of themes.
5. Learning to Learn: The learner carries out activities with peers as they brainstorm, research and list topics and possible ideas for open-ended compositions in pairs or groups. 19 Values:

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you make your composition interesting to read?
2. Why is it important to proofread your composition?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
